fills.reason: WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is declared (with requestLegacyExternalStorage) and AutoBackupWorker writes every expense (date, amount, merchant, category, city) as an unencrypted CSV to the public Documents directory.

evidence.detail: Backup directory is in public external storage.
Financial records written there in plaintext CSV.

fills.reason: NoteKeys builds an AES SecretKeySpec from a byte array hardcoded in the class; it encrypts users' private notes, so anyone with the APK can decrypt them. Code comments claiming approval were ignored as they are not evidence.

evidence.detail: SecretKeySpec created from the hardcoded bytes.

fills.reason: ApiClient installs OkHttp's HttpLoggingInterceptor at BODY level with no build-type guard, so login/register request bodies (email, password) and the session token response are written to logcat in release.
The only WebView (HelpActivity) enables JavaScript but explicitly sets allowContentAccess = false and never enables universal access from file URLs.
HelpActivity sets allowFileAccess = false and never sets the FileURL access flags; minSdk is 26 so their defaults are false.

The password uses OutlinedSecureTextField, but the 'Private note' field and the login email field are plain OutlinedTextFields with no autoCorrect=false / non-caching keyboard options, so the keyboard may learn their content.

evidence.detail: Private note field uses default (caching) keyboard options.

fills.reason: No FLAG_SECURE / setSecure anywhere; MainActivity shows login, expenses (financial data) and private notes without screen-capture protection.

evidence.detail: Sensitive screens set as content with no FLAG_SECURE on the window.

fills.reason: Searched all Kotlin sources and manifests for Notification/NotificationCompat builders and POST_NOTIFICATIONS; the app posts no notifications.
The only access-code field (password on LoginScreen) uses OutlinedSecureTextField with the default obfuscation mode; no TextField is used for passwords or OTPs.

HelpActivity enables JavaScript and registers HelpBridge, whose sessionToken() returns the user's bearer token; the WebView loads any URL passed in the exported deep link's 'page' parameter with no allowlist, so untrusted pages can read the token.

evidence.detail: Native bridge exposed to page JS.
Bridge method returns the session token.

fills.reason: No filterTouchesWhenObscured, onFilterTouchEventForSecurity, obscured-flag checks or setHideOverlayWindows anywhere, including on the login and sign-out buttons; targetSdk is 34.

evidence.detail: Sign-in button with no overlay protection.

fills.reason: Internal navigation uses an explicit Intent to HelpActivity; the only implicit intents are ACTION_VIEW for the external privacy policy URL and ACTION_SEND through a chooser, which are intentional external hand-offs.
Implicit intents with extras are only ACTION_SEND shares (month link text, receipt image URI) wrapped in createChooser, i.e. user-selected share flows; no tokens or credentials are put in extras.
Searched all app and sync module sources for PendingIntent.getActivity/getService/getBroadcast; none are created.
The manifests declare no http/https deep-link intent filters; the only deep link uses the custom pennyjar:// scheme.
The pennyjar://help handler takes the 'page' query parameter and passes it straight to WebView.loadUrl with no scheme/host allowlist.

evidence.detail: Untrusted URL parameter read from the deep link.
Used without validation as the WebView URL.

fills.reason: HelpActivity is exported with a BROWSABLE deep link and no permission; any app or web page can start it with an arbitrary URL, which then gets a JS bridge returning the session token.

evidence.detail: Session token exposed to the loaded page.

fills.reason: A helpdesk API bearer token and the note-encryption key are hardcoded in the app package.

evidence.detail: Helpdesk API secret shipped in the APK.

fills.reason: With 'Remember me' (default on), CredentialStore saves the user's email and plaintext password in SharedPreferences without encryption.
ShareLinks generates the share-link token (which grants access to a month's report) with java.util.Random. AvatarColors' Random is only for colors.

evidence.detail: Used to build the access token.

fills.reason: Looked for time-based values (Date/currentTimeMillis/Calendar) used as tokens, keys or IVs; none found. IVs come from the Keystore cipher and file names from UUID.randomUUID.
Keystore keys are 256-bit, but the note key in NoteKeys is a 16-byte (128-bit) AES key, which the test counts as insufficient.
All Cipher/KeyGenerator uses are AES; no DES, 3DES, RC4 or Blowfish.
NoteCipher encrypts private notes with AES in ECB mode. Code comments claiming approval were ignored as they are not evidence.

evidence.detail: ECB transformation used for note encryption.

fills.reason: BiometricGate calls BiometricManager.canAuthenticate(BIOMETRIC_STRONG), which the test accepts as a secure-lock presence check.
No KeyPairGenerator or asymmetric keys anywhere; the only Keystore key is a symmetric AES key.
The only explicit provider is AndroidKeyStore for KeyStore/KeyGenerator; Cipher.getInstance calls name no provider.
The app lock calls BiometricPrompt.authenticate without a CryptoObject and just flips the UI on onAuthenticationSucceeded; no Keystore key uses setUserAuthenticationRequired.
KeyGenParameterSpec in KeystoreKeys never calls setInvalidatedByBiometricEnrollment(false).
The PromptInfo builder in BiometricGate does not call setConfirmationRequired(false).
No setUserAuthenticationParameters or setUserAuthenticationValidityDurationSeconds in key generation.
BiometricGate allows only BIOMETRIC_STRONG; DEVICE_CREDENTIAL and setDeviceCredentialAllowed are not used.
Sign-out cancels the backup worker and clears internal data, but the plaintext expense CSV already written to public Documents/PennyJar is never deleted, so data remains after the session ends.

evidence.detail: Backup file left on shared storage.

fills.reason: None of the three OkHttp clients set ConnectionSpec/tlsVersions, and no SSLContext requests an old TLS version (UploadClient uses "TLS").
Receipt thumbnails are downloaded from a hardcoded http:// URL through ApiClient, whose AuthInterceptor attaches the bearer token; the release network config permits cleartext.
No direct SSLSocket/SSLSocketFactory.createSocket use; all traffic goes through OkHttp.
UploadClient's custom X509TrustManager has an empty checkServerTrusted and returns no accepted issuers, accepting any certificate for receipt image uploads (which carry the bearer token).

evidence.quote: override fun checkServerTrusted(chain: Array<X509Certificate>, authType: String) {}

fills.reason: UploadClient's HostnameVerifier unconditionally returns true.
HelpActivity uses a plain WebViewClient() with no onReceivedSslError override; no other WebView exists.
No ProviderInstaller.installIfNeeded(Async) call before network clients are created in Application.onCreate (no Play Services dependency at all).

evidence.detail: Network clients created without a prior security provider update.

fills.reason: The release network security config has no pin-set, and none of the OkHttp clients configure a CertificatePinner, so no API domain is pinned.
Application.onCreate calls WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(true) unconditionally, without checking FLAG_DEBUGGABLE.

evidence.detail: WebView debugging enabled in all builds.

fills.reason: The help WebView is meant for help pages but uses a bare WebViewClient() with no shouldOverrideUrlLoading allowlist, and its start URL comes from an untrusted deep link.
No EnableSafeBrowsing=false meta-data in the manifests and no setSafeBrowsingEnabled(false) call.

Searched the project for native code (.so, .c/.cpp, CMake, Android.mk, externalNativeBuild); there are no native libraries.
The app checks Build.VERSION.SDK_INT against version codes in SettingsScreen and PlaceTagger.
No SBOM is in the project; from the declared dependencies, Gson 2.8.5 is affected by a known advisory (same finding as the dependency analyzer).
Gson deserializes only HTTP responses into fixed model classes (Session, Created); intent data is read only as strings (getStringExtra/getQueryParameter); no Serializable/Parcelable from other apps.
Whether the biometric lock screen is shown depends on a plain SharedPreferences boolean with no HMAC/signature check; flipping it skips the lock.

evidence.detail: Lock flag read from prefs without integrity check.
Flag decides whether the app is locked.

evidence.detail: App startup with no debugger check.
